senses.gloss:
Dhṛtarāṣṭra
(‘One by whom the nation is supported’)
------------------------------------------
If धृतराष्ट्र had not been born, the world would have suffered an irreparable loss; because, there would then have been no Mahābhārata and hence no Bhagavadgītā either! Born blind, he was impervious to the sage advice of great sages and savants, including his best well-wishers. His infatuation for his arrogant son दुर्योधन was matched only by his hatred of the virtuous Pāṇḍavas. He was the very anti-thesis of what his name signifies.
He was the levirate-son of Vicitra-vīrya in अम्बिका by व्यास. Since he was sightless, he could not be made the king of हस्तिनापुर. His younger brother पाण्डु was hence crowned as the king.
He had married the eleven daughters of Subala, the king of गान्धार, of whom गान्धारी was the eldest and the chief queen.
When पाण्डु died prematurely and his children—the five Pāṇḍavas—were still young, धृतराष्ट्र took the reins of the kingdom and arranged for the proper maintenance and एदुचतिओन् of the Pāṇḍavas also along with that of his hundred sons.
When युधिष्ठिर, the eldest of the Pāṇḍavas was of proper age he was crowned as the yuvarāja (the crown-prince). Very soon, he became extremely popular with the subjects.
Egged on by दुर्योधन, the jealousy-incarnate, धृतराष्ट्र sent the Pāṇḍavas to Vāraṇāvata for a ‘change,’ where the former had plotted to kill them by arson. Due to the timely help of विदुर, the virtuous minister, the Pāṇḍavas escaped. Later on, they went to Virāṭanagarī, participated in the स्वयṁवर of the princess द्रौपदी and succeeded in marrying her.
Dhṛtarāṣṭra, on the advice of the grandsire भीष्म and others, called them back and gave them half the kingdom. The Pāṇḍavas started ruling it from their newly built capital इन्द्रप्रस्थ. Their prosperity and popularity roused the jealousy of दुर्योधन further, who managed to banish them to the forest by the well-planned stratagem of a game of dice exerting pressure on them through his ड़थेर्.
When the Pāṇḍavas had fulfilled all their commitments and sent Śrī कृष्ण as their emissary of peace, requesting for their share of kingdom or at least some means of maintenance, धृतराष्ट्र pleaded his helplessness, unable to control or influence his son दुर्योधन.
On the one hand, he was afraid of the impending war. On the other, he was hoping against hope that his sons would come out victorious!
After the war when all his sons and their comrades had been decimated, his anger, especially against भीम, manifested itself in a surreptitious attempt to crush him. However, Śrī कृष्ण’s forethought saved भीम from the tragedy.
Though he was looked after well, by the king युधिष्ठिर, problems of old age, repentance about past actions and the advice of the saintly विदुर induced him to take to the life of a वानप्रस्थ. He later perished in a forest fire.
See also MAHĀBHĀRATA.
